Skewered Drake (H73)

Region (English scoring-table division): Serpentspine.

In one sentence: Lead the black orcs and their drakon companions out of the old dwarven holds, turning a raiding tribe into a Drakonshan empire supported by drakon riders and subjects.

Story: High｜Mission-tree length: Long (43 direct missions across two stages)｜Mission-tree update: the local mission file was modified on 2026-07-09 and supports v1.37.5.0; the 2024 dev diary reflects the design at that time｜Uniqueness: Very high｜Tedium: Medium-high｜Early pressure: Medium-high｜Expansion ability: Very high

Identity and History

Skewered Drake (H73) is a black-orc tribe in the middle Serpentspine in 1444, not Wyvernheart in Escann. The country history file gives it a tribal government, Drakeclaw Orc culture, Old Dookan faith and the ruler Gashak. It is the historical rival of nearby Shadowdreamer. Current local flavour places its home, Gor Vazumbrog, in a dwarven hold ruined by the Purple Dragon disaster: the ancestors settled among the ruins, formed a long symbiosis with the local drakons and learned to tame them. The English offline Wiki dates the tribe's settlement in the hold to 894; that is a world-history date, not a current mission trigger.

The Chinese country name uses a term that can suggest a flying dragon; the English game files call the mount a Drakon. The Chinese name alone does not establish that these creatures can fly. The distinctive feature is the lasting partnership between orcs and mounts: drakons fight with the army, while their scales and bones also enter tool, armour and weapon production. The tension between population, mounts and cavern capacity drives the story of leaving the old hold.

National Story and Campaign Arc

The opening missions consolidate the middle Serpentspine: clear routes, defeat hostile orcs, seize dwarven legacies, tame more drakons and train riders. The exiled Zog and his Shadowdreamer followers are the local story's immediate rivals; the western underground roads and knowledge of Bulwar to the south reveal a hunting ground larger than the old lair. These are player-facing goals after mission progress, not conquests already completed in 1444.

The turning point is “Claim Dominion”. Completing it triggers an event that overwrites the country name as Drakonshan, changes the government to the Drakonshan Dominion and switches to the second half of the mission tree, while retaining Tag H73. From then on, raiding and carrying off loot are not enough: a state spanning the underground and surface needs roads, breeding dens, holds, mines and sustainable tribute. The latter missions bring cave trolls, dwarven lands and surface countries into a subject network, turning drakon riders from a strike force into instruments of overlordship.

Mechanics That Actually Define the Campaign

  1. Drakons and mythical cavalry: H73-specific events enable mythical cavalry mounted on drakons. Missions and events develop training and the ruler's mount, producing a high-impact underground raiding army. This is the route's central loop, not merely a normal cavalry bonus.
  2. Two-stage mission tree: Begin as a tribe opening underground routes and accumulating loot, then receive the imperial-stage missions after the renaming and government reform. The 43 direct missions are long because of this country-form transition and its parallel military, construction and subject routes.
  3. Drakonshan authority: The reform introduces a dedicated authority value from 0 to 100. It can be spent to levy subject labour, extract subject resources or hold tournaments. Resource extraction weakens subject provinces and raises their liberty desire, so coercion has a real governing cost.
  4. From raiding to management: Black-orc loot and underground expeditions drive the early expansion; repairing roads, developing mines, building drakon dens and managing subjects then support more mounts and wars. The loop demands both warfare and administration.
  5. A multi-people subject empire: The later missions encourage governing a wide area through subjects and drawing resources from them with authority. The final goals require a large subject network, extending beyond the middle Serpentspine toward Bulwar and farther east.

How a Campaign Unfolds

Early pressure comes mainly from underground colonisation, contests over routes and the accumulation of starting resources. Use drakon troops and black-orc raiding power to secure a foothold, then follow the underground roads to holds, metal and loot. The opening is not powerless, but missions, territory and government reform arrive progressively; sitting in the starting cavern stalls the main arc.

After entering the Drakonshan stage, secure the economy needed by elite cavalry and manage subjects, authority and liberty desire together. Moving south into Bulwar opens the surface route but also brings more complicated religious, cultural and great-power diplomacy. The final route still asks for wider overlordship and a large subject structure, so “very high expansion ability” does not mean low operational burden. Drakon training, mission unlocks, subject composition and distant wars repeatedly demand planning.

Formations and Endgame

“Skewered Drake → Drakonshan” is a renaming, reform and mission continuation of the same H73 country, so it remains one encyclopedia entry. The latter missions point toward a large overlord state maintained by drakon riders; that is a playable mission future, not a fixed outcome established by a historical map.

When the generic conditions are met, H73 can instead form Tarakar (M04). That decision changes the Tag; H73-exclusive mission visibility strictly requires H73, and the decision warns that the tree will be interrupted. It is an optional detour, not part of the main campaign. A few H73 events allow triggers to continue after “was H73, now M04”; this does not establish that the entire H73 tree is retained.

Personality and Recommendation

The v2.1 personality coordinates are Expansion 94/100｜Autocracy 88/100｜Magic↔Artifice 50/100 (100 = magic, 0 = artifice; theme intensity 25/100)｜Pluralism 45/100.

The v2.1 values profile is Neutral (44/100) with a stable trajectory. Forced submission, subject labour and development extraction are real forms of coercion, but their severity is lower than slavery, treating people as resources or extermination. Some practical details of the labour interactions still require in-game confirmation, so the country should not be pushed into the lowest values tier under the old model.

This route suits players who like black orcs, unusual cavalry, long-distance expansion from the underground to the surface, and the transition from raiding to a subject empire. It becomes tiring if you dislike waiting for underground expansion, complex subject management, or the very large territorial and subject thresholds in the second half.

Community Experience and Evidence Boundary

The 2024 official dev diary presents drakon companions, cavalry warfare and the route from the Serpentspine into Bulwar as design pillars. Two player accounts from the same year also praise the drakon and subject narrative; one mentions mission thresholds and a particular subject potentially blocking progress, while another's wonder issue may have been caused by a submod. These are period player experiences, not substitutes for current script conditions.

Identity, names, missions and mechanics in this entry follow the current local Mod and localisation. The offline Wiki did not return a dedicated H73 country page; only related pages for Gor Vazumbrog and Shadowdreamer were found, so detailed state formation remains unresolved. Intermediate-year projections and later-period overlays from the Halann historical map are not written as inevitable EU4 history.

National Ideas

The following reproduces the current local national-idea text and script effects. Traditions apply when the set is adopted; the seven ideas unlock in sequence as points are invested, and the ambition applies after all seven are unlocked. Only national ideas are listed: racial, government and mission bonuses are excluded. A successor idea set does not automatically stack with the earlier set. Idea descriptions may recall history or express future aspirations; they do not automatically establish events already completed in 1444. Names and complete descriptions use the current Mod’s English localisation. Alternative and predecessor/successor sets remain separately conditional, including whether new ideas are accepted on formation.

Effect units inherited from the source data are reproduced for parity, not revalidated here; suspicious percentages or script-valued effects require separate review. Raw script values are shown where appropriate.

Skewered Drake (H73) — Skewered Drake Ideas

Set ID: H73_ideas. Source: project-verified Mod script (public artifact omits local path and line offsets).

Applicability condition (source script):

    trigger = {
        tag = H73
    }

Skewered Drake Traditions

  • Cavalry recruitment cost: -20% (cavalry_cost; raw value -0.20).

  • Envoy travel time: -20% (envoy_travel_time; raw value -0.2).

1. Drakons

Born from the howling pit within Gor Vazumbrog, the scar left behind by the Hunter of the Deep's awakening, come the great Drakons upon which we ride. These beasts who were the apex predator of the middle Serpentspine, pending our arrival, are vicious creatures, naturally built for battle. Their reddish-black scales are as durable as diamonds, their bodies long and slender to weave between stalagmites with ease. Their pitch-black talons are capable of rending muscle and bone alike, doubling as tools with which to latch onto and run along the walls of the tunnels. The only way to make them more dangerous was to put our orcs upon them. Saddled upon these drakes we put our finest warriors to ride into battle causing devastating damage. As the drake tears through lines the orc finishes those left in its carnage, directing it from above to its next target.

  • Cavalry shock: +15% (cavalry_shock; raw value 0.15).

2. Visages Of Wrath

Of the many terrible sights one might encounter among the dark annals of the Serpentspine, few would dispute that a Drakon rider is among the most frightening. Covered in bioluminescent algae, menacing images of death and terror are sprawled across these mounts. In a flurry of colors and pictures, they dash by in the tunnels. Should you manage to avoid this blur of light, it was most likely at the whim of the orc above so that he may get the kill personally.

  • Morale damage: +10% (morale_damage; raw value 0.1).

3. Climbing Claws

Emulating the Drakons they ride, the Skewered Drake warriors have managed to fashion iron rakes that they can attach to their hands and latch onto walls with. Much like a Drakon can scale cliffs, now they can too. Climbing over walls, the Skewered Drake warriors are able to bypass defenses otherwise impenetrable.

  • Siege ability: +15% (siege_ability; raw value 0.15).

4. Great Skewers

To cook a drake, one often skewers it and roasts its chunks over a fire, proving tremendously difficult due to their size and the strength of their muscles. To overcome this, Skewered Drake have become masters at sharpening and crafting massive skewers to cook them and other beasts they come across. In fact, many orcs of the clan now carry these skewers around with them at all times when out traversing the Serpentspine; in numbers they are able to make camp with them by repurposing these skewers as palisades wherever they go.

  • National Supply Limit Modifier: +25% (global_supply_limit_modifier; raw value 0.25).

5. Tools of the Trade

The toughness of a drake's scales can not be understated; it is no wonder then that they would make such excellent tools. A drake's diamond-hard scales can be fashioned into a multitude of things, such as armor, but most importantly into pickaxes, hammers, and shovels. These tools are capable of mining tough ores and rocks, and should these tools ever chip or break there will always be more scales in short time.

  • Development cost: -10% (development_cost; raw value -0.1).

6. Fight Night

A regular sporting event held by the chieftains of the Skewered Drake, these so called 'Fight Nights' are where they pit two drakes up against each other in a battle to the death. To add to the fervor of the event, orcs are allowed to bet on the winner in the hopes of making quick coin. In the end, no matter who wins the fight or bets, the chieftain gets a cut of the pool and the clan gets that much richer from it.

  • National tax modifier: +10% (global_tax_modifier; raw value 0.1).

7. First and Finest

Gorrath may be known as the Wrathful but he was not merely a brute; he was also tremendously clever, utilizing the existing layout of the ruined hold to administrate efficiently and effectively. It is due to this that the Skewered Drake clan has managed to maintain stability for hundreds of years with relative ease whereas many of their brethren in the Serpentspine have failed.

  • Stability cost modifier: -15% (stability_cost_modifier; raw value -0.15).

  • Maximum Absolutism: +5 (max_absolutism; raw value 5).

Skewered Drake Ambition

  • Army tradition: +1 (army_tradition; raw value 1).

Tarakar (M04) — Tarakari Ideas

Set ID: M04_ideas. Source: project-verified Mod script (public artifact omits local path and line offsets).

Applicability condition (source script):

    trigger = { tag = M04 }

Tarakari Traditions

  • Infantry combat ability: +10% (infantry_power; raw value 0.10).

  • Available loot: +0.5 (available_province_loot; raw value 0.50).

1. Mountains Don’t Give Back What They Take

Bloodshed is all our people has ever known. Best our enemies and take everything they have, once merely to survive, but no longer now that the mountain-home and its wealth are orcishkind’s dominion. We will take from the strong, not because we need to, but because we are stronger.

Raids outside the Serpentspine will be overseen by the Algakar Code, which ensures fair treatment of prisoners until they are ransomed, forbids attacks on towns that haven’t finished rebuilding, and states that those who accept to pay tribute shall be left alone. The rules ensure the surfacers know what to expect of us, so that they give up as much riches as possible. But more importantly, they allow the weak to rebuild and grow richer. And once they gather enough wealth, we will take everything from them too, because we are stronger.

  • Aggressive expansion impact: -15% (ae_impact; raw value -0.15).

2. The Unchained

In the darkness of the Dwarovar, the trader and explorer needs light, but the raider prowls in the dark. Black orcs have invented many fighting techniques adapted to the darkness along the centuries, and the unification of orcishkind has refined them into a martial art of its own that foregoes reliance on sight entirely.

The greatest blademasters of that art undergo a ceremony in which they gouge out their own eyes to rely solely on Dookan’s sight instead of their own, and emerge Unchained. Even other orcs fear such masters; they whisper of seemingly impossible counters to attacks that were not even started, of a terrifying implacable fighting pace and believe them undefeatable in combat.

  • Discipline: +5% (discipline; raw value 0.05).

  • True faith tolerance: +1 (tolerance_own; raw value 1).

3. The True Treasure

Dookan teaches that thinking of war without keeping peace in mind is madness, and that thinking of peace without keeping war in mind is foolishness. There is a time for all things, and what truly keeps us together isn’t the glory we share in battle. It’s the family we come back to, and the smile of a son or daughter welcoming us home. One day, they too shall know war, but as Dookan teaches, there is a time for all things, and nothing is more sacred in Tarakar than a child’s innocence.

  • National unrest: -2 (global_unrest; raw value -2).

4. Rule of the Fittest

Everything. Everything one desires can be acquired in an Ozarm’chadash, ensuring he has the strength to claim it. Such is the informal rule of those duels the participants implicitly agree on.

Still, the nature of such a challenge makes people wary of issuing them unless they have nothing left to lose, and they don’t hone our people’s skills as much as they could. We will replace those duels of honor to settle disputes by ritualized gladiatorial combats to keep us strong. Anyone who wishes to acquire greater status, wealth, or fame can enter the arena to claim it, and the last one standing -even should it be a mean enough dwarf or the odd honorable goblin- will have earned it by right of strength, the only one that matters. Such is the way we orcs live by, and the only true way.

  • Army tradition: +0.5 (army_tradition; raw value 0.5).

  • Manpower from true faith provinces: +10% (manpower_in_true_faith_provinces; raw value 0.10).

5. Improve, Adapt, Overcome

“-That map of yours was right, Mushû. Tons of good salvage in there. The bearded really don’t make stuff as they used to. -I think of that often, answered Mushû the Philosopher, because they called him that for a reason. They fell apart because of all those giant halls they dug and giant statues they made to fill them. -You ain’t making any sense. -They were full of themselves. Wanted to be remembered, but only built their own tomb instead. We’ll make something out of it, and it’s going to be used by our people and not sitting there looking fancy. -Uh, never thought of it like that. Guess that’s why they call you the Philosopher. -Just remember, we’re giving new life to every piece we take back. We’re not just scavengers. We’re builders of the future. -Yeah, well, the future can wait a bit. These pieces are heavy.”

As they got to work, Gralk couldn't help but wonder if there was some truth to Mushû's words. Maybe they were more than just scavengers. Maybe, just maybe, they were part of something bigger.

  • global_regiment_cost: -10% (global_regiment_cost; raw value -0.10).

  • Construction cost: -10% (build_cost; raw value -0.1).

6. End of the Clans

To become Tarakar’s ruler, one must destroy all obstacles on their way. To rule Tarakar is to rule unchallenged. Orcs may once have followed local chiefs, but there is now only one being strong enough to be worth following under the mountains.

Our realm itself shall acknowledge that truth, and from bickering tribes something new, something stronger will be forged. Out of the blood spilt in unseen caverns and the fire of the Serpentspine’s forges, a true nation of orcs will emerge.

  • Maximum absolutism: +15% (max_absolutism_effect; raw value 0.15).

7. Breaking the Cage

We orcs hold within us the spark legated by Dookan himself, his divinity our own. A gift, but also a duty to free him from the unjust imprisonment inflicted upon him by the treacherous other gods as he wanted to find a new home for himself and us.

However, numerous variations of the story can be found all across the Serpentspine. We will work on compiling them and creating a unified version of the true teachings of Dookan, and orcish scholars will become Tarakar’s warriors in the greatest of all conflicts! Freeing a god is not a task that can be achieved by mortal steel; Dookan’s cage shall be broken by making the followers of the traitor gods turn away from them to weaken their power. Only then shall their treachery be undone!

  • Missionaries: +1 (missionaries; raw value 1).

  • Cost of enforcing religion through war: -50% (enforce_religion_cost; raw value -0.5).

Tarakari Ambitions

  • Reduced liberty desire in subjects on other continents: +1500% (reduced_liberty_desire_on_other_continent; raw value 15).
